description: Shared platform policy for converting mapped provider records into deterministic central DB upsert plans.
rules: Build ingestion records from provider_ingestion_mapping first.
Reject duplicate idempotency keys within the same batch.
Reject unsafe relative_path values using artifact_storage_policy.
The generated plan is metadata only; DB transactions and retries are executed by provider_ingestion_execution_policy.

FE-P0c (2026-05-26): condition_hash is propagated verbatim from compute_condition_hash; central writers must never recompute. operator AND recorded_by columns of measurement_attempts are populated from the same provenance source (FE-P0b req5).

Session parent row (2026-07-29, multichamber repair 2026-08-05): test_sessions is ingested FIRST in the same single-chamber/session transaction as its measurement children. New chamber traffic uses (provider_id, chamber_id, provider_session_id) as its natural key and derives the session uuid from the same scope; the reserved legacy sentinel preserves pre-multichamber rows and UUIDs. created_at/updated_at are omitted because the central schema defaults both to now(). Providers that already create the session row out of band may omit it from the batch.

Report parent row (2026-08-04): a non-empty report-output batch emits exactly one report_runs row after test_sessions and before report_outputs in the same transaction. The parent uses its caller-supplied deterministic id as the primary-key replay identity, requires provider/session/terminal completed evidence, and omits created_at because the central database owns its now() default. An empty report-output collection emits neither report_runs nor report_outputs.

Provider result identity (multichamber repair 2026-08-05): chamber result ids are scoped with the same chamber identity before they reach the central provider_result_id uniqueness boundary; legacy result ids remain byte-compatible.

FE-P0c (2026-05-26): coverage_by_condition_hash is a CENTRAL materialized view derived from measurement_attempts (FE-P0a) — ingestion writers MUST NOT include it in this plan and MUST NOT write to it directly.
